clue.text: Tall order in the army?

parts.note: read literally, a lofty or senior instruction-giving body within the military: the generals at the top who issue orders

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a demand in the army is unreasonably difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall order' looks like the idiom for an unreasonable demand, but 'tall' means elevated and 'order' means command.
explanation.definitionFit: The supreme leadership of armed forces, who issue the top orders, is known by this term.

clue.text: Rough boisterous action on stage?

parts.note: rowdy rough-and-tumble fun, with a whimsical second reading as a drama starring equine characters

explanation.surface: A critic describes a rowdy piece of physical theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a play about a stable animal would literally fit the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdy, rough fooling around is the everyday sense; the stage hint plays on the word as a theatrical piece about steeds.

clue.text: Information man had applicable to whole class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the facts a man possessed applied to an entire group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' is a link word joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to a whole group rather than one member is described this way, as opposed to specific.

clue.text: Carrying headgear submissively

definitions.meaning: literally holding one's hat in one's hand

explanation.definitionFit: Literally holding a hat in one's hand; idiomatically approaching humbly, like a supplicant asking a favour.

clue.text: Spoils hard tract of wetland

parts.note: mars means spoils or ruins
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Something ruins a firm stretch of boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or fen is a low-lying area of waterlogged ground.

clue.text: Win or draw

definitions.meaning: to win people over, gain their support
to draw in, pull towards oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to pull in or gain interest or support, as a crowd-puller does with an audience.

clue.text: Author unhappy about including word of hesitation

indicators.note: including means the reversed word takes in the hesitation word in its middle
about tells us the word for unhappy is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: sad means unhappy
um is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A writer is dejected about saying 'er' too often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SAD into DAS, and 'including' puts UM inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist who wrote The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: Warning from enchantress

definitions.meaning: an alarm device sounding an alert, as on a fire engine
a seductive woman, after the mythical sea nymphs who lured sailors

explanation.definitionFit: An alarm that wails as an alert; also the Greek mythical singer luring sailors to wreck, hence a seductress.

clue.text: Whisky soup?

parts.note: facetiously read as a broth made from Caledonian spirit, though it is really a hearty barley and mutton soup

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a bowl of soup made from whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: the dish contains no whisky, only the name of the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional barley, vegetable and mutton soup from north of the border, named after its country as is the whisky.

clue.text: One not entitled to a full wage

definitions.text: One not entitled to a full wage

parts.words: One not entitled to a full wage
parts.note: describes a worker on reduced hours, paid accordingly, rather than someone being cheated

explanation.surface: A worker complains about being denied full pay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests injustice, but the person simply works fewer hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed for only some of the working week earns a correspondingly smaller wage.

clue.text: Come back lighter for second contest

parts.note: return means come back
a match is something used to light a fire

explanation.surface: Someone asks a smoker to come back with a lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch between the same opponents is the follow-up contest after a first game.

clue.text: Go too far with surplus production

definitions.meaning: to exceed a limit or boundary
an excess quantity printed or manufactured beyond what was needed

explanation.definitionFit: To exceed limits, as an invading army or a late meeting does; also extra copies printed beyond the order.

clue.text: Principle ready with earphones

parts.note: the setter means principal, the head of a school, as in headteacher
set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

explanation.surface: A principle is ready to go along with some earphones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the clue prints 'Principle' for the homophone 'Principal', the head of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones worn over the ears, often with a microphone attached, are known by this name.

clue.text: Clio moving about with inner pain

indicators.note: moving signals that the letters of Clio are rearranged

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Clio, the muse or the car, moving about while suffering stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges CLIO to COLI; 'with' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe abdominal pain caused by intestinal spasm, familiar from crying babies, is an internal ache.

clue.text: He provides notes about girl travelling to a rocky height

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: travelling shows that the two letters of to are moved around

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone writes notes about a girl journeying up a craggy hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link; 'travelling' turns TO into OT. A TOR is a rocky peak found in English moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: A commentator who adds explanatory remarks to a text is the person meant.

clue.text: Up-to-date resort according to publication

parts.note: new means up-to-date
a spa is a health resort
per means according to, as in per the rules

explanation.surface: A trendy holiday spot, according to some publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily periodical of news and features is a printed publication.

clue.text: Target man upsetting shrewish woman

indicators.note: upsetting signals that the letters of the phrase are overturned into a new order

explanation.surface: A nagging woman aims to upset a particular man.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh-tempered, overbearing scold is a shrewish woman.

clue.text: Main view perhaps comes from outstanding feature

definitions.meaning: the main is the sea, so a window looking over a sea inlet
a window that literally stands out from a house wall

explanation.definitionFit: A projecting window that juts from a wall stands out, and might give a view across a coastal inlet.

clue.text: Make an impression with one initially misty photograph

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word misty

parts.note: a print is a photograph

explanation.surface: A photographer makes an impression with a single hazy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp or press a mark into a surface is to leave an impression.

clue.text: Sporting get-together?

parts.note: a rugby formation where forwards bind together, read as a social gathering for sports fans

explanation.surface: An invitation to a sports club social evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the pun: the players literally get together, heads down, in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, forwards bind and push against each other to restart play; also a disorderly crowd.

clue.text: Grab some grains first to be used as flood protection

indicators.note: first puts the grains ahead of the word for grab

parts.note: sand is a mass of tiny grains
to bag something is to grab it

explanation.surface: Advice to seize some grit before the flood comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be used as' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacks filled with grit are stacked as barriers to hold back rising water.

clue.text: Organisation with widespread influence found at sea

definitions.meaning: a sprawling body with tentacles reaching everywhere

explanation.definitionFit: An eight-armed sea creature; figuratively, a powerful body whose reach extends in all directions like tentacles.

clue.text: Lit up fancy bulb

indicators.note: fancy signals an elaborate rearrangement of the letters of lit up

explanation.surface: A decorative light bulb is switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' looks electrical, but it is the plant kind.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring flower, famous in Holland, grows from a bulb.

clue.text: New story first from French author

indicators.note: first puts the story ahead of the letter for new

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A French writer produces a fresh tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Francoise Sagan was the French novelist who wrote Bonjour Tristesse.

clue.text: Write name on a book or flag

parts.note: to pen means to write
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Instructions to write a name on either a book or a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A long tapering flag, flown on ships or awarded to sports champions, is a kind of banner.

clue.text: Keeping back possession that has increased

parts.note: a holding is a possession, such as land or shares
up means increased, as in prices are up

explanation.surface: An investor hangs on to an asset that has risen in value.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaying or detaining something, as traffic is held, means keeping it back.

clue.text: Bold old lines on the tree

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway network
the ash is a tree

explanation.surface: Daring old verses written about a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link. BR, British Rail, ran Britain's railway lines until privatisation in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means cheekily self-assertive, which is a brazen kind of daring.

clue.text: Obvious privilege?

parts.note: patent can mean obvious, so a plainly evident entitlement, really a legal monopoly on an invention

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on an entitlement so plain nobody questions it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obvious' suggests a clear advantage, but it hints at the legal document for inventions.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclusive legal entitlement to exploit an invention, granted by the state, is this privilege.
